summary.text: Wayne Rogers, a Democrat who has been executive assistant to the Jefferson County sheriff since 2019, lost the November 3, 2026 election for secretary of state of Alabama to Caroleene Dobson.
A first-time candidate, he is an attorney who has practiced in Alabama since 1988.

paragraphs.text: Rogers is a native of Thomasville and has lived in Birmingham for 45 years. He earned a B.A. in music from Samford University in 1984 and a J.D. from Samford's Cumberland School of Law in 1988.
As a litigator he appeared in court in 66 of Alabama's 67 counties. He joined the Jefferson County Sheriff's Office in 2019 and is also a former chair of the Jefferson County Democratic Party.

Rogers serves on the boards of several mental-health entities, including the JBS Mental Health Authority, and on the national board of Crisis Intervention Team International. He and his wife, Lauri Sutton Rogers, have been married for 38 years and have three grown children.
During the campaign, he listed ending straight-ticket voting, adopting early voting and letting absentee voters fix ballot defects as his key messages.
He received 45.4% of the vote to Caroleene Dobson's 54.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
